clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby exempt the said William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through January 31, 1940, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when January 31, 1940 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period. Executive Order No. 8326, signed January 22, 1940, is a later event and not an end: its operative sentence reads "I hereby further exempt the said William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending July 31, 1940." It grants William S. Garland a further exemption for six months ending July 31, 1940; it does not revoke or shorten this order, and under the owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md an extension is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7995 of October 28, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 210566, Common Crawl capture 2026-01-16T02:40:31Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7995, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on January 31, 1940; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8326 (January 22, 1940); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).

savings.reason: The order grants a permission for a fixed period and contains no saving or transfer provision. What it left behind, William S. Garland's continued federal employment during the period, accrued while the period ran; no duty or right continues after January 31, 1940 by the order's own terms. Any exemption after January 31, 1940 rests on the separate later order(s) recorded as later events.
